name: Wistia
summary: Video hosting built for marketing — player customisation, viewer analytics and lead capture.
best_for: marketing teams who want video on their own site with real analytics and lead capture, and who care that the player does not recommend a competitor's video afterwards
skip_if: you just need somewhere to put videos — an unlisted upload to a free platform does that, and the reason to pay here is the analytics and the branding control, not the hosting
honest_knock: Bandwidth is the meter that decides your bill, and it is the one number you cannot predict before you publish. A single video that does well can move you from Free to Business in a month, which is arguably the product working — but budget for it rather than being surprised. Their FAQ, as read on 19 September 2026, was precise about which way it cuts: free accounts cannot exceed their bandwidth limit, while paid plans are billed for usage beyond what is included or prepaid. The free tier carries Wistia branding on the player, so it is a trial with no time limit rather than a plan you can ship a brand on. The published prices are the annual ones; the page's toggle sits on Annual with a 20% saving and the month-to-month figures are not in its source, so a monthly subscriber cannot price the plan from the pricing page. The webinar overages were the sharpest edge on that reading: $2.00 per extra minute means a session that runs long costs real money, the allowance is per event rather than cumulative, and the shortened FAQ of 19 October 2026 no longer prints either figure, so confirm them before you book a long session.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-19 on wistia.com/pricing, Video Platform tab; the monthly-toggle rates below are from the 19 September 2026 reading and were not re-read, because the page renders them rather than writing them into its source) Four tiers, and the headline numbers are the ANNUAL rates: the billing toggle on the page is set to Annual with a “Save 20%” chip, so Business at $79 a month and Business + Signals at $329 a month are what you pay when you commit for a year. On 19 September 2026, with the toggle set to Monthly, the same three cards read $0, $99 and $412 a month, with the per-extra-user rate moving from $25 to $31. Since that reading Wistia has renamed the $329 tier from Business + Lead gen to Business + Signals and added an AI credit allowance to every card; the prices, storage, users and bandwidth did not change. Free $0: 25 GB storage, 1 user, 200 GB bandwidth, 3,000+ lifetime credits, basic analytics, Wistia branding on the player. Business $79: 250 GB+ storage, 3+ users, 1 TB bandwidth, 5,000+ monthly credits, branding removed, collections and playlists, CTAs and forms, advanced analytics. Business + Signals $329 is Business plus Signals — marketing-automation integrations (HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot), video engagement data on contact records, automated lead scoring, audience segmentation, triggered email nurtures, sales alerts and pipeline and revenue attribution — and the FAQ calls Signals an add-on for the Business plan that is included with every webinar plan. Enterprise is quote-only: from 1 TB storage, 2 TB bandwidth, custom users, 12,500+ monthly credits, Signals, team accounts, SSO, video playback protection, a dedicated customer success manager. Price per additional user $25. Dubbing and AI audio descriptions are an add-on on both Business cards and included only on Enterprise. The page does not say what a credit buys. Storage beyond the plan is prepaid upfront or billed as usage. The FAQ as read on 19 September 2026 also said bandwidth resets monthly and is billed as usage past the allowance on paid plans (free accounts are hard-capped instead), and priced webinar overages at $0.20 per extra attendee and $2.00 per extra minute, per event; the shortened FAQ of 19 October 2026 repeats neither, so treat both as the last confirmed reading rather than current page text. You can cancel at any time unless you are on Enterprise or a signed order form, either at the end of the billing cycle or immediately, and no refund is issued either way. Webinar plans have their own tab on the same page and carry no price in the source.

vendor_mcp.what: Server for uploading video, making bulk updates, managing access and reading performance data from your agent. Every action asks for approval by default; you can set a tool to always-approve or block it.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their FAQ: "All Wistia accounts have access to Wistia's MCP server... no upgrade needed." Anything you can do in the app you can do through the server; you only upgrade for more product features. Restricted by role rather than plan — owners and managers only.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
